Put a block of titles above the table

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_titles.Rd

plan_titles() gives the title lines printed above the table on each page, in the body of the page and the width of the content — not the section header, which is the page's own furniture. One block serves every page; pages gives each page its own. The plan attaches them as the pages' rtf_titles attribute, which rtf_tables() prints as rtf_titles() does.

Usage

plan_titles(.plan, ..., pages = NULL, border = NULL)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

...

The rows of one block, used on every page: strings, one a line, or a character vector of them.

pages

A list with one block per page, when the pages do not share one. Give ... or pages, never both: a three-row title on a three-page table cannot be told apart from three one-row titles.

border

NULL (default) for none, or an rtf_border() for the title block as a whole on every page of this table, read as rtf_titles()(border = ) is: top above the first row, bottom below the last row, inside_h between rows, left / right on every row. It is this table's own, so it wins over the document's rtf_titles()(border = ) and rtf_style()(titles = list(border = )). It is drawn with rtf_style(title_format = "table"); the text form ignores it, with a warning.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb; plan_footnotes() for the block below; plan_paginate_group() (heading_at = "title") for a title line named after each page's value.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_total()

Examples

tbl <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c("Subjects", "Age, mean (SD)"),
  Placebo   = c("86", "75.2 (8.59)"),
  Active    = c("84", "75.7 (8.29)"))

# Minimal: two title lines on the one page
pages <- table_plan(tbl) |>
  plan_titles("Table 14.1.1", "Demographics") |>
  plan_apply()
attr(pages[[1]], "rtf_titles")
#> [1] "Table 14.1.1" "Demographics"

# A page per laboratory parameter, each with its own table number
lab <- data.frame(
  PARAM   = rep(c("ALT (U/L)", "AST (U/L)"), each = 2),
  Visit   = rep(c("Baseline", "Week 4"), 2),
  Placebo = c("22.1", "23.0", "25.4", "24.8"),
  Active  = c("21.8", "30.2", "24.9", "29.1"))
pages <- table_plan(lab) |>
  plan_paginate_group(col = "PARAM", keep = FALSE) |>
  plan_titles(pages = list(c("Table 14.3.1", "Alanine aminotransferase"),
                           c("Table 14.3.2", "Aspartate aminotransferase"))) |>
  plan_apply()
lapply(pages, attr, "rtf_titles")
#> $`ALT (U/L)`
#> [1] "Table 14.3.1"             "Alanine aminotransferase"
#> 
#> $`AST (U/L)`
#> [1] "Table 14.3.2"               "Aspartate aminotransferase"
#>
